fi-rhinomuraena-quaesita.title: Blue Ribbon Eel
fi-rhinomuraena-quaesita.summary: A thin, ribbon-shaped moray rated expert-only.
rows: About 50 in; wild record 130 cm (51.2 in) TL (FishBase)
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia and French Polynesia; including Marianas and Marshalls
notes: Prefers low light and stays near the bottom.

fi-gymnothorax-nigromarginatus.title: Blackedge Moray
fi-gymnothorax-nigromarginatus.summary: A brown moray with small pale spots and a dark fin edge from the Gulf of Mexico. Like all morays it is a strong predator that needs a large, tightly covered tank.
rows: No: leaves corals alone but eats small fish, shrimp and crabs
Carnivore: live or thawed frozen shrimp, clams, squid and small fish such as silversides
Western Atlantic: southern Florida to Texas and Yucatán; seagrass beds and banks at 10–100 m
notes: Needs plenty of live rock to hide among; best in a large fish-only tank.

fi-gymnothorax-favagineus.title: Tesselata Moray (Laced / Honeycomb Moray)
fi-gymnothorax-favagineus.summary: A huge Indo-Pacific moray with a honeycomb pattern of black spots on pale skin. It is a powerful predator that eventually needs a very large, secure aquarium.
warn: Grows very large; plan for a very big aquarium.
